title: Autofocus sharpens the wrong fragment
summary: Phase-gradient autofocus handles smooth low-order defocus but barely improves high-order random phase error and can make the measured impulse-response width worse.
trigger: Apply correlated random phase error up to five radians RMS, then run the same PGA configuration used for quadratic defocus.
observed: At five radians RMS the reported recovery is 0.89x: azimuth IRW changes from 0.3096 to 0.3461 even while entropy falls.
invariant: Autofocus improvement must survive multiple focus metrics; a lower entropy alone cannot validate a fragmented point response.
fix: Report entropy and IRW together, retain the losing regime, and limit the recovery claim to measured low-order phase error.

timeline.title: Increase phase complexity
timeline.detail: Random correlated structure replaces the smooth phase gradient PGA estimates well.

timeline.title: Optimize a partial signal
timeline.detail: Entropy improves while the dominant lobe no longer represents the full target response.

timeline.title: Make two metrics disagree
timeline.detail: IRW worsens to a 0.89x recovery even though entropy continues downward.

timeline.title: Narrow the claim
timeline.detail: The release claims near-diffraction recovery only for low-order defocus.

limits: The raw phase history and targets are simulated under stripmap, broadside, straight-and-level geometry.
